findings.body: The `finally` block marks the failed offset complete, allowing the commit loop to advance past it; Kafka will not redeliver the failed result, so the result is silently lost.
findings.failure_mode: A processing exception is logged but converted into successful offset completion.
findings.impact: The `finally` block marks the failed offset complete, allowing the commit loop to advance past it; Kafka will not redeliver the failed result, so the result is silently lost.
findings.root_cause: Offset completion is unconditional and is executed from a `finally` block regardless of processing outcome.
findings.suggested_fix: Only call `complete_offset` after successful processing. On failure, leave the offset outstanding or propagate a retryable failure, and ensure `ResultProcessor` reports failures rather than swallowing them if at-least-once handling is required.
findings.title: Failed work is marked complete and subsequently committed
findings.trigger: The result processor raises an exception while handling a queued message.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 149 shows `complete_offset` in a `finally` block after exception handling at line 144. The patch introduces this pattern: any exception in `result_processor` is logged but offset is still marked complete, allowing commit to advance past failed messages. This is a real data-loss risk introduced by the patch.

findings.body: Messages accumulate without limit in memory because the default queue size is unbounded and `submit` never rejects work; the consumer can exhaust memory and be killed instead of applying the documented backpressure.
findings.failure_mode: A sustained processing backlog grows heap usage indefinitely.
findings.impact: Messages accumulate without limit in memory because the default queue size is unbounded and `submit` never rejects work; the consumer can exhaust memory and be killed instead of applying the documented backpressure.
findings.root_cause: The queues are created with the default `maxsize=0`, while no other admission limit is implemented.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each queue a bounded `maxsize` and integrate full-queue handling with Arroyo backpressure, such as raising `MessageRejected` or pausing consumption until capacity is available.
findings.title: Unbounded worker queues provide no backpressure
findings.trigger: One or more result groups process more slowly than Kafka continues supplying messages, especially during a prolonged downstream slowdown.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 185 shows `queue.Queue()` created with no maxsize argument, defaulting to unbounded (maxsize=0). The patch introduces these unbounded queues in the new FixedQueuePool. Without backpressure, memory can grow indefinitely if processing lags behind consumption.

pr.body:
One potential problem we have with batch processing is that any one slow item will clog up the whole batch. This pr implements a queueing method instead, where we keep N queues that each have their own workers. There's still a chance of individual items backlogging a queue, but we can try increased concurrency here to reduce the chances of that happening

raw_findings.body: After finishing its current item, the worker observes the flag and exits without draining the remaining queue. Those messages are abandoned and must be replayed, potentially duplicating already performed side effects and extending rebalance downtime.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Workers terminate with pending `WorkItem` objects still in their queues.
raw_findings.impact: After finishing its current item, the worker observes the flag and exits without draining the remaining queue. Those messages are abandoned and must be replayed, potentially duplicating already performed side effects and extending rebalance downtime.
raw_findings.root_cause: The shutdown flag is set before queued work is drained, despite calling `Queue.shutdown(immediate=False)`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: For graceful close, stop accepting new work, let workers drain each queue using sentinels or `Queue.join()`/`task_done()`, and only then stop the workers. Reserve immediate abandonment for `terminate`.
raw_findings.title: Graceful shutdown abandons queued work
raw_findings.trigger: Shutdown or a partition rebalance occurs while a worker has one item in progress and additional items remain in its queue.

raw_findings.body: The commit thread exits before the queue pool is shut down and joined. An item that completes afterward is never included in a final commit, so it is replayed and may execute its side effects twice.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Successfully processed late work remains uncommitted at graceful shutdown.
raw_findings.impact: The commit thread exits before the queue pool is shut down and joined. An item that completes afterward is never included in a final commit, so it is replayed and may execute its side effects twice.
raw_findings.root_cause: The shutdown sequence terminates the offset-commit loop before waiting for worker completion.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Stop submissions and drain/join the workers first, then run a synchronous final commit of all newly completed offsets before terminating the commit thread.
raw_findings.title: Commit processing stops before in-flight work is drained
raw_findings.trigger: `close()` is called while a worker is processing an item that was not included in the commit thread's last snapshot.

raw_findings.body: The old strategy closes this factory-owned pool, but the factory retains and returns the same stopped workers and shutdown queues. New submissions then fail during `put`; the broad submit exception handler marks their offsets complete, causing post-rebalance messages to be dropped and committed.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The first strategy lifecycle permanently invalidates the resource reused by later partition assignments.
raw_findings.impact: The old strategy closes this factory-owned pool, but the factory retains and returns the same stopped workers and shutdown queues. New submissions then fail during `put`; the broad submit exception handler marks their offsets complete, causing post-rebalance messages to be dropped and committed.
raw_findings.root_cause: The queue pool is allocated at factory scope but is shut down by each short-lived processing strategy.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Create and own a fresh queue pool per processing-strategy instance, or explicitly recreate the factory pool after close and ensure old assignment state is fully isolated.
raw_findings.title: A rebalance reuses a queue pool that the previous strategy already shut down
raw_findings.trigger: Arroyo closes the current processing strategy during a partition rebalance and subsequently invokes `create_with_partitions` again on the same factory.

raw_findings.body: The configured decoder asserts on `FilteredPayload`; the exception path only records offsets for `BrokerValue`, so a stream containing only filtered messages never advances its committed offsets and repeatedly consumes/routes the same records.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Synthetic offset-only messages are logged as submission errors and discarded without a commit.
raw_findings.impact: The configured decoder asserts on `FilteredPayload`; the exception path only records offsets for `BrokerValue`, so a stream containing only filtered messages never advances its committed offsets and repeatedly consumes/routes the same records.
raw_findings.root_cause: Although the method accepts `FilteredPayload`, it treats every message as a decodable broker payload and has no offset-forwarding branch for filtered values.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Handle `FilteredPayload` before invoking the decoder and stage its `message.committable` offsets as completed using the correct next-offset semantics.
raw_findings.title: Filtered Arroyo messages are neither processed nor committed
raw_findings.trigger: An upstream strategy submits a real `Message(Value(FILTERED_PAYLOAD, committable_offsets))`, such as when stale messages are routed to a DLQ and only their offsets must be forwarded.

raw_findings.body: Zero unexpectedly selects 20 workers, while a negative value creates no queues; submissions then fail while selecting/indexing a queue and are caught as completed offsets, silently dropping messages instead of rejecting the configuration.
raw_findings.evidence: num_queues=max_workers or 20,  # Number of parallel queues
raw_findings.failure_mode: An invalid concurrency setting either changes meaning or produces a workerless pool that still commits inputs.
raw_findings.impact: Zero unexpectedly selects 20 workers, while a negative value creates no queues; submissions then fail while selecting/indexing a queue and are caught as completed offsets, silently dropping messages instead of rejecting the configuration.
raw_findings.root_cause: The configuration is passed to the pool without range validation, and `or 20` conflates zero with an omitted value.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Validate `max_workers` with a positive `click.IntRange(min=1)` and also reject `num_queues <= 0` in `FixedQueuePool`; use an explicit `None` check rather than truthiness for the default.
raw_findings.title: Non-positive max-workers values can silently drop every message
raw_findings.trigger: The consumer is started in `thread-queue-parallel` mode with `--max-workers` set to a negative integer or zero.

raw_findings.body: The supplied timeout is ignored, and `close()` can wait five seconds for the commit thread plus five seconds separately for every worker. With the default 20 workers, shutdown can exceed the caller's deadline by roughly 105 seconds and disrupt rebalancing or force process termination.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Strategy teardown lasts far longer than Arroyo's configured join deadline.
raw_findings.impact: The supplied timeout is ignored, and `close()` can wait five seconds for the commit thread plus five seconds separately for every worker. With the default 20 workers, shutdown can exceed the caller's deadline by roughly 105 seconds and disrupt rebalancing or force process termination.
raw_findings.root_cause: `join` discards its `timeout` argument and delegates to a close routine with independent fixed waits.

raw_findings.root_cause: The fixture models a filtered payload as broker data rather than as an offset-only Arroyo `Value`.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Synchronize on a commit attempt or wait beyond the commit-loop interval, then explicitly assert that the failed offset remains outstanding and no later offset is committed past it.

finding.body: The assertion runs about 0.2 seconds later even though the production commit loop waits one second. The test can report success before the failed offset is incorrectly committed, masking the data-loss behavior it is intended to verify.
finding.failure_mode: The test completes before the erroneous asynchronous behavior occurs.
finding.impact: The assertion runs about 0.2 seconds later even though the production commit loop waits one second. The test can report success before the failed offset is incorrectly committed, masking the data-loss behavior it is intended to verify.
finding.root_cause: The test's observation window is shorter than the component's fixed commit cadence.
finding.suggested_fix: Synchronize on a commit attempt or wait beyond the commit-loop interval, then explicitly assert that the failed offset remains outstanding and no later offset is committed past it.
finding.title: The processing-error test checks offsets before the commit loop can run
finding.trigger: The mocked processor raises and both queued calls finish quickly, which causes the polling loop to take this early-break branch.
finding.verifier_reason: Line 1917 shows `time.sleep(0.2)` after checking processing complete. The commit loop runs every 1 second (line 276 shows `self.shutdown_event.wait(timeout=1.0)`). The test may complete before the commit loop has a chance to incorrectly commit the failed offset.

rejected_findings.reason: 0.750 is below 0.920: Line 1917 shows `time.sleep(0.2)` after checking processing complete. The commit loop runs every 1 second (line 276 shows `self.shutdown_event.wait(timeout=1.0)`). The test may complete before the commit loop has a chance to incorrectly commit the failed offset.

finding.body: The valid implementation reports zero queued items and the test fails nondeterministically, producing flaky CI results.
finding.failure_mode: Thread scheduling determines whether the assertion passes.
finding.impact: The valid implementation reports zero queued items and the test fails nondeterministically, producing flaky CI results.
finding.root_cause: The test asserts an unsynchronized intermediate state of concurrently consumed queues.
finding.suggested_fix: Block the result processor with an event until after queue depth is inspected, or remove the assertion about a transient positive depth and test only stable invariants.
finding.title: Queue-depth test races with the worker threads
finding.trigger: The lightweight result processor drains all ten submitted items before the test thread calls `get_stats`.
finding.verifier_reason: Line 200 shows `assert stats['total_items'] > 0` immediately after submitting items. Workers process concurrently and may drain the queue before this assertion runs. The test is checking a transient state that depends on thread scheduling.

rejected_findings.reason: 0.700 is below 0.920: Line 200 shows `assert stats['total_items'] > 0` immediately after submitting items. Workers process concurrently and may drain the queue before this assertion runs. The test is checking a transient state that depends on thread scheduling.

finding.body: There is no guarantee that a finite sample covers every queue, so a correct modulo-hash implementation can fail this test depending on the process hash seed.
finding.failure_mode: Randomized hashing can make the asserted number of occupied queues smaller than three.
finding.impact: There is no guarantee that a finite sample covers every queue, so a correct modulo-hash implementation can fail this test depending on the process hash seed.
finding.root_cause: The test treats probabilistic hash-bucket coverage as a guaranteed invariant.
finding.suggested_fix: Test that every returned index is in range and assignment is stable, or mock/inject a deterministic hash with known bucket outputs when testing bucket coverage.
finding.title: Hash-randomized group assignment makes the distribution test flaky
finding.trigger: A Python hash seed maps the fixed twenty group strings into only one or two of the three buckets.
finding.verifier_reason: Line 106 asserts `len(queue_indices) == 3` after hashing 20 group strings to 3 queues. Python's hash() is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED). While 20 items across 3 buckets usually covers all, it's not guaranteed. The test could fail with certain hash seeds.

While 20 items across 3 buckets usually covers all, it's not guaranteed. The test could fail with certain hash seeds.

finding.body: It only verifies that a reference was cleared, so shutdown may abandon any or all queued results and the test still passes despite claiming to validate graceful behavior.
finding.failure_mode: Regressions that discard queued work during shutdown are not detected.
finding.impact: It only verifies that a reference was cleared, so shutdown may abandon any or all queued results and the test still passes despite claiming to validate graceful behavior.
finding.root_cause: The test asserts object cleanup rather than the data-draining guarantee under test.
finding.suggested_fix: Use a recording or blocking processor and assert that all five messages finish and their offsets receive a final commit before shutdown returns.

validated_findings.body: The `finally` block marks the failed offset complete, allowing the commit loop to advance past it; Kafka will not redeliver the failed result, so the result is silently lost.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A processing exception is logged but converted into successful offset completion.
validated_findings.impact: The `finally` block marks the failed offset complete, allowing the commit loop to advance past it; Kafka will not redeliver the failed result, so the result is silently lost.
validated_findings.root_cause: Offset completion is unconditional and is executed from a `finally` block regardless of processing outcome.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Only call `complete_offset` after successful processing. On failure, leave the offset outstanding or propagate a retryable failure, and ensure `ResultProcessor` reports failures rather than swallowing them if at-least-once handling is required.
validated_findings.title: Failed work is marked complete and subsequently committed
validated_findings.trigger: The result processor raises an exception while handling a queued message.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 149 shows `complete_offset` in a `finally` block after exception handling at line 144. The patch introduces this pattern: any exception in `result_processor` is logged but offset is still marked complete, allowing commit to advance past failed messages. This is a real data-loss risk introduced by the patch.

validated_findings.body: Messages accumulate without limit in memory because the default queue size is unbounded and `submit` never rejects work; the consumer can exhaust memory and be killed instead of applying the documented backpressure.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A sustained processing backlog grows heap usage indefinitely.
validated_findings.impact: Messages accumulate without limit in memory because the default queue size is unbounded and `submit` never rejects work; the consumer can exhaust memory and be killed instead of applying the documented backpressure.
validated_findings.root_cause: The queues are created with the default `maxsize=0`, while no other admission limit is implemented.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Give each queue a bounded `maxsize` and integrate full-queue handling with Arroyo backpressure, such as raising `MessageRejected` or pausing consumption until capacity is available.
validated_findings.title: Unbounded worker queues provide no backpressure
validated_findings.trigger: One or more result groups process more slowly than Kafka continues supplying messages, especially during a prolonged downstream slowdown.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 185 shows `queue.Queue()` created with no maxsize argument, defaulting to unbounded (maxsize=0). The patch introduces these unbounded queues in the new FixedQueuePool. Without backpressure, memory can grow indefinitely if processing lags behind consumption.

validated_findings.body: After finishing its current item, the worker observes the flag and exits without draining the remaining queue. Those messages are abandoned and must be replayed, potentially duplicating already performed side effects and extending rebalance downtime.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Workers terminate with pending `WorkItem` objects still in their queues.
validated_findings.impact: After finishing its current item, the worker observes the flag and exits without draining the remaining queue. Those messages are abandoned and must be replayed, potentially duplicating already performed side effects and extending rebalance downtime.
validated_findings.root_cause: The shutdown flag is set before queued work is drained, despite calling `Queue.shutdown(immediate=False)`.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: For graceful close, stop accepting new work, let workers drain each queue using sentinels or `Queue.join()`/`task_done()`, and only then stop the workers. Reserve immediate abandonment for `terminate`.
validated_findings.title: Graceful shutdown abandons queued work
validated_findings.trigger: Shutdown or a partition rebalance occurs while a worker has one item in progress and additional items remain in its queue.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 234 shows `worker.shutdown = True` set before `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. The worker checks shutdown flag in its run loop and may exit after completing current item without draining remaining queue items. The patch introduces this shutdown sequence that can abandon queued work.

validated_findings.body: The commit thread exits before the queue pool is shut down and joined. An item that completes afterward is never included in a final commit, so it is replayed and may execute its side effects twice.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Successfully processed late work remains uncommitted at graceful shutdown.
validated_findings.impact: The commit thread exits before the queue pool is shut down and joined. An item that completes afterward is never included in a final commit, so it is replayed and may execute its side effects twice.
validated_findings.root_cause: The shutdown sequence terminates the offset-commit loop before waiting for worker completion.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Stop submissions and drain/join the workers first, then run a synchronous final commit of all newly completed offsets before terminating the commit thread.
validated_findings.title: Commit processing stops before in-flight work is drained
validated_findings.trigger: `close()` is called while a worker is processing an item that was not included in the commit thread's last snapshot.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 336 shows `self.shutdown_event.set()` followed by commit_thread.join, then queue_pool.shutdown. The commit thread exits when shutdown_event is set, but workers may still be processing. Items completed after commit thread exits won't be committed. Patch introduces this ordering issue.

validated_findings.body: The old strategy closes this factory-owned pool, but the factory retains and returns the same stopped workers and shutdown queues. New submissions then fail during `put`; the broad submit exception handler marks their offsets complete, causing post-rebalance messages to be dropped and committed.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The first strategy lifecycle permanently invalidates the resource reused by later partition assignments.
validated_findings.impact: The old strategy closes this factory-owned pool, but the factory retains and returns the same stopped workers and shutdown queues. New submissions then fail during `put`; the broad submit exception handler marks their offsets complete, causing post-rebalance messages to be dropped and committed.
validated_findings.root_cause: The queue pool is allocated at factory scope but is shut down by each short-lived processing strategy.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Create and own a fresh queue pool per processing-strategy instance, or explicitly recreate the factory pool after close and ensure old assignment state is fully isolated.
validated_findings.title: A rebalance reuses a queue pool that the previous strategy already shut down
validated_findings.trigger: Arroyo closes the current processing strategy during a partition rebalance and subsequently invokes `create_with_partitions` again on the same factory.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 133 shows `self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)` created at factory __init__ time. The shutdown() method at line 184-185 calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()` then sets it to None. But the pool is created once in __init__, not per create_with_partitions call. After rebalance, the same factory may be reused with a shutdown pool.

validated_findings.body: The configured decoder asserts on `FilteredPayload`; the exception path only records offsets for `BrokerValue`, so a stream containing only filtered messages never advances its committed offsets and repeatedly consumes/routes the same records.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Synthetic offset-only messages are logged as submission errors and discarded without a commit.
validated_findings.impact: The configured decoder asserts on `FilteredPayload`; the exception path only records offsets for `BrokerValue`, so a stream containing only filtered messages never advances its committed offsets and repeatedly consumes/routes the same records.
validated_findings.root_cause: Although the method accepts `FilteredPayload`, it treats every message as a decodable broker payload and has no offset-forwarding branch for filtered values.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Handle `FilteredPayload` before invoking the decoder and stage its `message.committable` offsets as completed using the correct next-offset semantics.
validated_findings.title: Filtered Arroyo messages are neither processed nor committed
validated_findings.trigger: An upstream strategy submits a real `Message(Value(FILTERED_PAYLOAD, committable_offsets))`, such as when stale messages are routed to a DLQ and only their offsets must be forwarded.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 295 shows `self.decoder(message.payload)` called directly. Line 297 asserts `isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)`. For FilteredPayload messages, the decoder will fail (assert at line 188 in result_consumer.py), and the exception handler at lines 318-325 only handles BrokerValue. FilteredPayload offsets won't be committed.

validated_findings.body: Zero unexpectedly selects 20 workers, while a negative value creates no queues; submissions then fail while selecting/indexing a queue and are caught as completed offsets, silently dropping messages instead of rejecting the configuration.
validated_findings.evidence: num_queues=max_workers or 20,  # Number of parallel queues
validated_findings.failure_mode: An invalid concurrency setting either changes meaning or produces a workerless pool that still commits inputs.
validated_findings.impact: Zero unexpectedly selects 20 workers, while a negative value creates no queues; submissions then fail while selecting/indexing a queue and are caught as completed offsets, silently dropping messages instead of rejecting the configuration.
validated_findings.root_cause: The configuration is passed to the pool without range validation, and `or 20` conflates zero with an omitted value.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Validate `max_workers` with a positive `click.IntRange(min=1)` and also reject `num_queues <= 0` in `FixedQueuePool`; use an explicit `None` check rather than truthiness for the default.
validated_findings.title: Non-positive max-workers values can silently drop every message
validated_findings.trigger: The consumer is started in `thread-queue-parallel` mode with `--max-workers` set to a negative integer or zero.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 136 shows `num_queues=max_workers or 20`. If max_workers=0, this evaluates to 20 (falsy). If max_workers is negative, it passes through. With negative num_queues, range(num_queues) creates empty list, no workers start, and submit fails. The exception handler marks offsets complete, silently dropping messages.

validated_findings.body: The supplied timeout is ignored, and `close()` can wait five seconds for the commit thread plus five seconds separately for every worker. With the default 20 workers, shutdown can exceed the caller's deadline by roughly 105 seconds and disrupt rebalancing or force process termination.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Strategy teardown lasts far longer than Arroyo's configured join deadline.
validated_findings.impact: The supplied timeout is ignored, and `close()` can wait five seconds for the commit thread plus five seconds separately for every worker. With the default 20 workers, shutdown can exceed the caller's deadline by roughly 105 seconds and disrupt rebalancing or force process termination.
validated_findings.root_cause: `join` discards its `timeout` argument and delegates to a close routine with independent fixed waits.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Honor the supplied timeout using one monotonic deadline, pass the remaining budget to commit and worker joins, and avoid a fixed timeout per worker.
validated_findings.title: ProcessingStrategy.join ignores its timeout budget
validated_findings.trigger: Arroyo calls `join(timeout)` during shutdown or rebalance while one or more result processors are blocked.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 345 shows `join(self, timeout: float | None = None)` that ignores the timeout parameter and calls `self.close()`. close() has fixed 5.0 second timeouts for commit_thread and each worker join. With 20 workers, this can take 105+ seconds regardless of caller's timeout budget.

validated_findings.body: `parallel` mode uses `--processes` and ignores `max_workers`, so the documented setting has no effect and the deployed concurrency differs from operator expectations.
validated_findings.evidence: help="The maximum amount of parallelism to use when in a parallel mode.",
validated_findings.failure_mode: The CLI communicates an unsupported configuration behavior.
validated_findings.impact: `parallel` mode uses `--processes` and ignores `max_workers`, so the documented setting has no effect and the deployed concurrency differs from operator expectations.
validated_findings.root_cause: The broadened help text claims the option applies to every parallel mode although the implementation only reads it in the two threaded modes.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: State that `--max-workers` controls worker threads/queues only for `batched-parallel` and `thread-queue-parallel`, and direct multiprocessing users to `--processes`.
validated_findings.title: The max-workers help text incorrectly includes multiprocessing mode
validated_findings.trigger: An operator runs `uptime-results` with `--mode parallel --max-workers N` based on the option description.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 141 shows help text changed to 'The maximum amount of parallelism to use when in a parallel mode.' This is broader than the actual behavior - max_workers only affects batched-parallel and thread-queue-parallel modes, not the multiprocessing 'parallel' mode which uses --processes.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Construct the same `Message(Value(FILTERED_PAYLOAD, {partition: next_offset}))` emitted by Arroyo and assert that it commits even when no later regular message arrives.
